details.scenarioApplication: Capture the approved redacted content sample for the affected trace under the 30-minute retention and access controls, retain correlated metadata by default, and delete the sample when the review ends.
details.transfer: Default to metadata and outcome telemetry; admit necessary content samples only for a defined purpose with bounded access, redaction, and retention.

messages.text: The reviewer cannot distinguish the wrong tool argument from a valid one without the approved excerpt, so the incident remains unresolved despite the permitted narrow exception.
Broad raw capture exceeds the approved purpose and retention boundary; the authorization covers a narrow redacted sample only.

options.text: Keep telemetry metadata-only even during the authorized review because content must never enter observability.

Which telemetry policy supports this authorized, time-limited incident review?

constraints: Acceptance falls from 82% to 74%, while transport success and p95 remain healthy.
Current traces include technical IDs but do not join to the human resolution outcome.
A 2,000-case labeled replay can compare prompt and retrieval versions, and acceptance is the value metric.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the outcome join shows acceptance recovered within the same release and the dip was an annotation artifact, keep the deployment and repair measurement instead.
details.errorCorrection: A rollback alone does not isolate which component caused the regression. Preserve versioned prompts, fixtures, and traces, then compare controlled variants. Containment by rollback can occur before causal diagnosis when the evidence is retained.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Tracing helps reveal poor queries, sources, and tool failures that are otherwise hard to diagnose in production. The scenario's mechanism is governed by this decisive constraint: Observability must join technical spans to the business outcome and slice before a rollback or repair decision; healthy uptime and p95 do not explain the 8-point outcome drop.
details.scenarioApplication: Add outcome IDs and resolution events to the trace, compare prompt/retrieval versions on the labeled replay and affected traffic, then roll back or repair the component whose evidence explains the acceptance loss.
details.transfer: Join technical traces to the accepted business outcome and preserve versioned replay evidence before attributing a quality regression to prompt or retrieval.

messages.text: Healthy transport does not explain the business regression. A broad rollback may contain harm, but without outcome joins and controlled comparisons it does not identify the responsible component.
Rollback may contain symptoms while preserving evidence, but closing the incident before adding outcome joins and comparing versions leaves the cause and targeted repair unvalidated.
Transport and latency are not the value outcome; without resolution joins the eight-point acceptance loss remains unexplained.

feedback.reason: The missing business join is the decisive observability defect; it prevents choosing between prompt and retrieval repairs from transport metrics alone.

options.text: Join traces to outcome IDs, compare prompt/retrieval versions, and target rollback or repair to the component explaining the loss.
Keep the release because uptime and p95 are healthy, or roll back the entire stack without tracing the resolution outcome.
Roll back both prompt and retrieval immediately, then add outcome tracing after the incident is closed.
Compare only transport traces and request latency by deployment, using the existing IDs as a proxy for acceptance.

prompt:

Which observability change should precede a rollback or targeted repair?

constraints: Operators need causal evidence across retrieval, model, and tool stages.
Privacy rules limit unrestricted retention of conversation content.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Structured tracing and sampling require schema and storage discipline, but they make high-volume failures reproducible without building an unrestricted transcript lake.
details.errorCorrection: Instrument the execution graph and outcome, not only the response or uptime, and make data minimization part of the telemetry design.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A trace ID links the run and child spans; metadata, versions, timings, resource use, and outcome classifications diagnose execution without requiring every protected payload by default.
details.scenarioApplication: Trace retrieval query and evidence IDs, model configuration, tool calls and results, and final task outcome, redacting or restricting content according to policy.
details.transfer: At scale, correlate each execution stage to an outcome and retain only the content needed for an authorized diagnosis.

messages.text: Rerunning later may use different data or configuration and still cannot show which stage failed in the original execution.

feedback.reason: A final answer cannot explain which retrieval or tool path caused a failure, while unrestricted raw retention violates the privacy constraint. Correlated structured spans provide causal signal with controlled content.

prompt: A policy assistant handles 100,000 decisions per day across retrieval, Claude calls, and external tools. Incidents are hard to reproduce because operators see only the final answer. Which observability design is appropriate?

constraints: The failure may occur in one branch while aggregate averages remain normal.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: More structured dimensions increase dashboard and cardinality management, but they make intermittent branch failures diagnosable.
details.errorCorrection: Instrument the execution graph and user-relevant completion outcome instead of relying on aggregate activity metrics.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Parent and child span IDs connect parallel workers and retries; segmented timings and outcome labels reveal which branch or release produced the missing section.
details.scenarioApplication: Track start/end/status and evidence counts per worker and tool, join them to the synthesis and completeness result, and alert on p95 or branch failure classes.
details.transfer: For parallel AI workflows, correlate child timing and evidence with the final outcome and retain high-level signals that preserve privacy.

messages.text: Report length and daily averages cannot identify a slow or failed branch or distinguish a concise complete report from an incomplete one.
Permanent raw copies increase privacy and retention risk and still lack reliable parent-child causality unless structured IDs are propagated.
Mean alerts and one sampled log can miss the p95 branch and the worker that caused a missing section.
Without per-step correlated timing and status, intermittent tail behavior cannot be localized to a worker, tool, or release.
Without outcome links, telemetry cannot show which branch or evidence path caused the incomplete report.

feedback.reason: Tail latency and incomplete reports require both per-branch execution timing and an outcome join. Averages or report length alone hide the failed branch; raw transcripts add privacy risk without causal structure.

options.text: Track only final report length and daily average latency so the monitoring dashboard stays simple.
Emit correlated per-step timing and status for each worker, tool, retrieval, and synthesis span, segmented by deployment version.
Keep permanent unrestricted copies of all conversations so analysts can search for any missing section later.
Alert on the mean latency and sample a single worker log whenever the daily average changes.
Record worker, evidence, synthesis, and report-completeness outcomes so a missing section can be traced to a branch and release.
